facts.title: Domestic work made monumental
facts.body: Vermeer’s Milkmaid (c. 1660) raises a kitchen task to quiet grandeur — light, bread, and a steady pour.

facts.title: Concentration as virtue
facts.body: The maid’s downcast focus turns labor into dignity; Vermeer refuses satire and chooses respect.

facts.title: A ribbon of white
facts.body: Milk streams in a careful arc — time slowed to the thickness of paint.

facts.title: Crusts catching light
facts.body: Broken bread on the table gleams with tiny pointillés of highlight — still life inside a genre scene.

facts.title: Daylight from the left
facts.body: Cool window light models every fold of cloth and every plaster nick on the wall.

facts.title: A wall that breathes
facts.body: Nail holes and stains on the plaster make the kitchen feel lived-in — perfection without polish.

facts.title: Warmth on the floor
facts.body: A foot warmer rests below — comfort and, in Dutch emblem books, a possible hint of desire kept near the kitchen.

facts.title: Delft along the skirting
facts.body: Blue-and-white tiles run the baseboard — a humble frieze of domestic Delftware.
